title: Credential adapter answer
description: What a credential adapter prints on its standard output, once, as one JSON document. An adapter is a program of the machine's, started by the gateway outside the enclosure, that contains what one kind of host needs, such as a source code host: it mints or fetches a secret and defines how the secret is used, because hosts differ in that and Forager contains nothing specific to any host. It exits 0 with this document, or not 0 with a line on standard error. The gateway ignores a member that this schema does not define, in the document and in each apply item, unless a must_understand lists it: the document's, or the item's. A new member that narrows where, when or with which token the secret is set must be listed in must_understand.

token.description: The secret, for every apply entry that has none.

expires_at.description: When the secret stops working, RFC 3339. The gateway runs the adapter again five minutes before. Absent means it does not expire.

apply.description: Where the secret goes. Run again, an adapter returns the same hosts, schemes and paths: they are fixed when the run starts, and only the secret changes.

scheme.description: bearer sets Authorization: Bearer and the secret. basic sets Authorization: Basic with username and the secret as the password. header sets the header whose name is in header to the secret. The set is closed: an adapter chooses among what the gateway implements.

paths.description: The paths of these hosts the credential is set on, in the policy's path grammar: a path from the root, matched whole, or up to a final * matched as a prefix, where a segment written exactly {} matches one segment that is not empty: /repos/example-org/app/pulls/{} matches /repos/example-org/app/pulls/12 and not /repos/example-org/app/pulls/12/merge. A { or } anywhere else fails validation. A request to such a host on a path no credential of the host matches gets no credential, and under enforce passes only when the policy's egress.paths for the host match it. Several credentials may share a host when each has paths and no path of one overlaps a path of another; a credential without paths is alone on its hosts. Absent means every path.

push_ref.description: The one ref a git push through this item may create, update or delete, in full, such as refs/heads/qory/wi_01. The gateway reads the ref commands of every git-receive-pack to the item's hosts before it sends anything, and returns 403, without sending the push, for a push that names any other ref. For an item without push_ref, every push gets 403.

must_understand.description: The members of the item that the gateway must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the item, such as /push_ref. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines for an item; an item of a list is its index. A document with an item whose must_understand lists a pointer to a member that the gateway does not define is refused.

placeholders.description: Variables the enclosure gets with a value that is no credential, for a program that needs one set to start: the proxy replaces what the program sends.

must_understand.description: The members of the document that the gateway must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the document, such as /apply/0/push_ref. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines; an item of a list is its index. A document whose must_understand lists a pointer to a member that the gateway does not define is refused.
